# AppShell

The frame of an application (D88): a header row over a sidebar and a `<main>` that each scroll on their own, filling the viewport (`100dvh`). Because the header has a row of its own and `main` is its own scroller, nothing scrolls under the header, so a focused element is never obscured by it (WCAG 2.2 *Focus Not Obscured*) without `scroll-padding`. `main` carries `id={mainId}` and `tabIndex={-1}`: the target of a `SkipLink`, not a tab stop; focused by the skip link it draws the shared focus ring inside its box. A closed sidebar is `hidden`, not narrowed to icons; there is no responsive drawer and no stored open state, so this is a desktop frame. A page whose document must scroll as a whole does not use `AppShell`. Mount it at the root of the page with no margin or padding around it: it is `100dvh` tall, so anything around it makes the document scroll and slides the frame. Do not place a `ToastRegion` at `top-start` in an app with a skip link: the native top layer paints over the focused link. A theme can make `main` a surface beside a one-colour header and sidebar, with no CSS of the consumer's (D110): `--psi-app-shell-bg`, which must equal the canvas of the theme on the header and the sidebar, `--psi-app-shell-main-bg` and `--psi-app-shell-main-radius`. All three paint nothing by default. The corner is square unless a header and a sidebar both meet `main`. Put the header under that theme with `data-psi-theme` on the `NavBar`, whose rest props land on its `<header>`, and remove its line with `--psi-navbar-border-width: 0`. `main` pads the page from `--psi-app-shell-main-padding-inline` and `--psi-app-shell-main-padding-block`, 24px by default (D113); set both to `0` if your page pads itself. A page that wants a maximum width sets `max-inline-size` itself: `.psi-container` would add a gutter of its own. The sidebar draws a line on its inline-end edge when `--psi-app-shell-sidebar-border-width` is `1px`; it is `0` by default, and its colour is `--psi-app-shell-sidebar-border` (D114). Geometry set on the shell's root, in the page's theme or at `:root` reaches a sidebar or header under its own theme: a sub-theme declares only colour tokens again (D139). `<NavBar brandAlign="sidebar">` in `header` lines its brand up with the sidebar: the brand spans the sidebar's width and a leading 32px `IconButton` with a 16px icon puts it on the sidebar's icon column (D140). The sidebar insets its tree by `--psi-app-shell-sidebar-padding`, 8px.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `skipLink` | `ReactNode` | — | no | A `SkipLink` (D88), rendered first so it is the first tab stop. Point its `href` at `#` plus `mainId`. |
| `header` | `ReactNode` | — | no | The header row, usually a `NavBar` (D88). It sits in a row of its own above the sidebar and `main`, so nothing scrolls under it. |
| `sidebar` | `ReactNode` | — | no | The sidebar's content, usually a `NavTree` (D88). The shell wraps it in a `<div>`, not an `<aside>`: a `NavTree` is already the landmark. |
| `banner` | `ReactNode` | — | no | One page-level `Banner`, or several, rendered inside `<main>` before the page (D113). It sits edge to edge: its wrapper cancels main's padding on three sides, and the page starts one block padding below it. It scrolls with the page. A value that renders nothing, such as `stale && <Banner …/>`, takes no space. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | no | The page, rendered inside `<main>` (D88). |
| `sidebarOpen` | `boolean` | true | no | Whether the sidebar is shown. Controlled: wire your Menu toggle's `aria-expanded` and this to one piece of state. Closed, the sidebar is `hidden`, so it leaves the layout and the accessibility tree, and stays in the DOM so the toggle's `aria-controls` keeps naming an element (D88). |
| `sidebarMotion` | `"instant" \| "slide"` | instant | no | How the sidebar opens and closes (D142). `"instant"` shows and hides it at once, as before. `"slide"` runs its column to 0 and back, fading it, with main's corner following, over `--psi-app-shell-sidebar-duration` and `--psi-app-shell-sidebar-ease`, which alias the `move` motion preset (200ms, `--psi-ease-soft`); `prefers-reduced-motion` makes it instant. The prop never takes a time: retime it with those two tokens. Closed under `"slide"`, the sidebar is `visibility: hidden` rather than `hidden`: it leaves the tab order and the accessibility tree when the close ends, and is reachable as soon as an open starts. Its content sits in one inner `<div>` that scrolls, held at the sidebar's width so nothing reflows while the column moves: code that scrolls the sidebar must scroll that wrapper, not the element with `sidebarId`. With no `sidebar` content it is the instant frame. |
| `sidebarTheme` | `string` | — | no | A theme name for the sidebar alone, such as `"dark"`: sets `data-psi-theme` on the sidebar element, so every token inside re-resolves under that theme while the rest of the page keeps its own (D88). The sidebar paints `--psi-bg-primary` itself; a theme paints no background. Its `color-scheme` follows the theme, so its scrollbars do too (D116). |
| `sidebarId` | `string` | sidebar | no | `id` of the sidebar element, which a toggle names with `aria-controls` (D88). |
| `mainId` | `string` | main | no | `id` of `<main>`, which a `SkipLink`'s `href` names (D88). |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS class name(s) merged onto the component's root element. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | — | no | Forwarded ref to the root `<div>`. |

## Keyboard & assistive tech

| Keys | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Tab | The first stop is the skip link (when given), then the header, the sidebar's links and buttons, and the links of main, in document order. The shell adds no stop of its own: main has tabIndex={-1}. |
| Enter (on the skip link) | Follows the fragment href: focus moves to main, drawing the shared focus ring inside its box, and the next Tab continues from main's first link. |

A grid filling the viewport: the header sits in a row of its own and main is its own scroller, so nothing scrolls under the header and a focused element is never obscured by it (WCAG 2.2 Focus Not Obscured) without scroll-padding, which does nothing on a main that is not the document's scroller (D88). main carries id={mainId} and tabIndex={-1}, the skip link's target. A closed sidebar is `hidden`, so it leaves the layout and the accessibility tree while its id stays in the DOM for a toggle's aria-controls; the toggle's aria-expanded and sidebarOpen are wired by the consumer, since the shell is controlled and stores nothing. The sidebar is a div, not an aside: the NavTree inside is already the navigation landmark. sidebarTheme sets data-psi-theme on the sidebar alone, so its tokens re-resolve under that theme in a page that keeps its own; the sidebar paints --psi-bg-primary itself. Desktop frame only: no responsive drawer. Do not place a ToastRegion at top-start in an app with a skip link. main's rounded corner (--psi-app-shell-main-radius, D110) keeps the skip link's ring: the inset outline follows the curve, measured in Chromium in LTR and RTL. A `banner` renders inside main, before the page, so its action is a tab stop there; Banner is not a live region, so showing one announces nothing (D113).

## Theming

Override `--psi-app-shell-*` custom properties at any scope.



## Rules

- One accent per visual group; everything else neutral or ghost.
- danger only for actions with real consequences.
- Sizes are px numbers (24|32|40|48), never S/M/L.
- Typography tokens are --psi-text-{size}-{lineHeight}-{weight}.
- Override component tokens (--psi-{component}-*), not semantic tokens, for one-off theming.
- --psi-button-font overrides button typography across all sizes (documented D34 override; ember → mono).
- Wrap labeled form controls in Field — label association, description/error line, aria-describedby and aria-invalid come wired; don't hand-roll label+message rows.
- Field is for a control with a *visible* label. A toolbar filter control named by aria-label or placeholder takes neither a Field nor a hand-rolled label row — compare filter-toolbar (no labels) with table-pagination ("Rows per page" visible, so Field). Filters with visible labels submitted together by a Find button are filter-form: a Toolbar as="form" align="start" of Fields with one-line labels, where a field's error line is the Field's own and hangs below its control (D87, D92).
- Label beside its control: <Field labelPosition="start"> for one field in a toolbar or pager (keep Toolbar align="center"); <FieldStack labelPosition="start"> for a form whose labels share one column, as wide as the longest label up to --psi-field-label-max-width, stacking below 480px of the form's width. A theme sets --psi-field-label-align: end to put labels against their controls (D115).
- Width of a control: <Field controlWidth={80|120|160|240|320|480}> sizes the control it wraps in px and lets it shrink in a narrower column; the label and message keep the Field's width. Pick the step from the value: at size 32 an Input fits about 7/12/17/26/36/55 digits (an ICCID's 20 digits → 240; a page-size Select → 80). Without it the control fills the Field. A FieldStack stops at --psi-field-stack-max-width (640px). In a Toolbar, the control of a top-labelled Field without controlWidth takes --psi-toolbar-control-width (200px), as a bare control does, so filter-form and date-range-filter rows are even; controlWidth replaces it, and a side-labelled Field (Rows per page) keeps its content width (D135).
- A popup's maximum height is --psi-popup-max-height (320px), shared by every popup through its own alias (--psi-menu-max-height, --psi-combobox-popup-max-height); past it the popup scrolls. Override the alias for one component, the shared token for all (D131).
- Select for a short fixed list; Combobox when the list is long enough to search, or more than one value is picked (D130). Combobox takes options as data ({value, label, description?, disabled?}), filters as the user types, and with multiple shows the picked values as Tags. Select has no multiple.
- Use Dialog for blocking modal flows — title/footer slots, dismissible gate; danger stays on the footer Buttons, one accent per group.
- Text links are Link (React) or the .psi-link class on any <a>: accent colour, underlined at rest, never by colour alone (D119). A router app passes its own link as Link's only child. Button href is for an action that should look like a button. Inside a NavItem or among NavBar's links, pass your router link itself, not Link.
- Pick between Tabs, SegmentedControl and RadioGroup by the job (D132). Switch 2–4 views of one region compactly (Map/Trace, Preview/Code): <Tabs> with a <SegmentedControl aria-label> (no value: Tabs owns it) of <Segment>s in place of TabList, outside the TabPanels, plus a TabPanel per segment. Switch page sections, more than 4 views, or a vertical list: Tabs + TabList + Tab. Pick one of 2–4 short options that applies at once (Light/Dark/System, a theme): <SegmentedControl aria-label value onValueChange>, a radio group wherever it sits (value makes it one). A value a form submits, options with descriptions, or more than 4: RadioGroup (Select for many). An action: Button or Toolbar. Segment labels are one or two words; the control never wraps, and truncates them when its container is narrower; fill shares the width equally. Sizes 24|32|40.
- A count after a label is Count (D124): neutral by default; tone="attention" is a pill and should carry a label ("4 stuck"), since the tone is visual. A Count is never a live region. In a NavTree, pass it as NavItem's count, and an icon as icon on NavItem or NavGroup; the icon is decorative and sized by the tree.
